```{python}
import polars as pl
import requests #new for reading in JSON
import io       #new for reading in JSON
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)
```


```{python}
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
response = requests.get(url)
df = pl.read_json(io.BytesIO(response.content))
```

## QUESTION 1

1. __Convert values to missing__ Start with a fresh copy of the flights dataset by reading it in from the link provided above (as opposed to starting with the dataset you ended with in the last assignment). Identify data values that are problematic, non-sense or impossible and change them to be missing. In your report include one record example (one row) from your clean data, in the raw JSON format. Your example should display at least one missing value so that we can verify it was done correctly. (Note: JSON will convert NaN's to null). Describe your process for finding values that needed to be changed, and how you changed them.

I used the describe() to look through the values inside the table one by one and then searched if their were any values that were off or didn't seem right to be in the data set. Then I used the pl.when and .then and other methods in order to adjust the data to make it match the requirements described in the question.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
fixed = df.with_columns(
  pl.when(pl.col("airport_name") == ("")).then(None).otherwise(pl.col("airport_name")).alias("airport_name"),
  pl.when(pl.col("num_of_delays_late_aircraft") == (-999)).then(None).otherwise(pl.col("num_of_delays_late_aircraft")).alias("num_of_delays_late_aircraft"),
  pl.when(pl.col("minutes_delayed_nas") == (-999)).then(None).otherwise(pl.col("minutes_delayed_nas")).alias("minutes_delayed_nas"),
  pl.when(pl.col("month") == ("n/a")).then(None).otherwise(pl.col("month")).alias("month")

)
print(fixed.filter(pl.col("airport_name").is_null()).head(1).write_json())

```

## QUESTION 2

2. __Filling in missing data__ For all the "minutes_delayed" columns, fill in any missing values with the median of that column. For the "num_of" columns, fill in missing values with that column's mean.

_Nothing to write/report for this question_

```{python}
minutes_cols = [c for c in fixed.columns if c.startswith("minutes_delayed")]
num_of_cols = [c for c in fixed.columns if c.startswith("num_of")]

filled = fixed.with_columns(
    *[pl.col(c).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False).fill_null(pl.col(c).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False).median()) for c in minutes_cols],
    *[pl.col(c).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False).fill_null(pl.col(c).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False).mean()) for c in num_of_cols]
)
```

## QUESTION 3

3. __Display a histogram for num_of_delays_carrier and for minutes_delayed_nas (2 separate histograms in total). Comment on the shape of each one. Also report the mean of each of these columns now that missing values have been filled in.__

Both histograms are skewed to the right (positively skewed). Most airports and months have a pretty low number of carrier delays and low NAS delay minutes, but there is a long tail on the right side from a smaller number of observations with very high values meaning that they are outliers in the data set. After filling in missing values, the mean of `num_of_delays_carrier` and `minutes_delayed_nas` are: 
Mean of num_of_delays_carrier: 691.29
Mean of minutes_delayed_nas: 69682.66

```{python}
p1 = (ggplot(filled, aes(x="num_of_delays_carrier"))
    + geom_histogram(bins=30)
    + labs(title="Distribution of Number of Carrier Delays",
           x="Number of Delays (Carrier)",
           y="Count"))
p1.show()

p2 = (ggplot(filled, aes(x="minutes_delayed_nas"))
    + geom_histogram(bins=30)
    + labs(title="Distribution of Minutes Delayed (NAS)",
           x="Minutes Delayed (NAS)",
           y="Count"))
p2.show()

print(f"Mean of num_of_delays_carrier: {filled['num_of_delays_carrier'].mean():.2f}")
print(f"Mean of minutes_delayed_nas: {filled['minutes_delayed_nas'].mean():.2f}")
```
